conventions.convention: An IPM uses a nonempty class of real measurable functions integrable under both measures, takes the supremum of absolute integral differences, and may be infinite; separation is not assumed.
Critics are anchored at x₀ and are 1-Lipschitz. The signed objective is the data integral minus the generated-law integral, giving a negative sign in the generator gradient.
The local-Lipschitz branch requires one parameter neighborhood and one integrable envelope valid for every pair of parameters there on a single measurable full-measure latent set.

The gradient formula is conditional on value-function Fréchet differentiability, attainment by the chosen signed optimal critic, and almost-everywhere Fréchet differentiability of its generator composite with measurable derivative. Compact dual attainment is not asserted.
Almost-everywhere differentiability of the value assumes full AC through the Euclidean Rademacher supplier; the preceding continuity and envelope estimates assert no choice use.
Jensen–Shannon divergence includes a factor of one half on each KL term and uses natural logarithms.
Counterexample probability weights are pₙ = 2⁻ⁿ for n ≥ 1. The density-based gradient witness assumes Countable Choice for its Lebesgue interval-measure supplier.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated compact metric data space and measurable generator family with almost-sure parameter continuity and measurable pairwise distances, V(θ) = W₁ˣ(μ,Pθ) and V is continuous. Under the common-neighborhood integrable-envelope hypothesis, V is locally Lipschitz with constant ∫Kθ₀ dρ on the specified neighborhood. At a point satisfying the additional value differentiability, signed critic attainment, and composite differentiability hypotheses, ∇V(θ₀) = −∫∇θHθ₀(θ₀,z) dρ(z).
For probability measures P,Q and a nonempty class F of real measurable functions integrable under both, d_F(P,Q) := sup over f ∈ F of |∫f dP − ∫f dQ| ∈ [0,+∞].

seams_checked.note: Checked the supplier's coupling definition, normalized signed KR statement and proof against the consumer uses. The WGAN theorem retains nonempty compact metric spaces, Borel probabilities, anchoring and the infimum coupling convention.
